the use of bifidobacterium phytases in foods for human consumption would be beneficial, but further research on the bioavailability of minerals and on the safety aspects is needed.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
bifidobacteria are a promising source of phytases, which can be purified and used in the production of infant cereals.

the bifidobacterial enzymes are effective to dephosphorylate phytate in infant cereals and to increase mineral solubility, but their application in food processing should be further investigated to optimize the process conditions and to assess the effect on the final product.

the application of B. pseudocatenulatu m and B. longum spp. infants phytases in the infant cereal matrix is effective in reducing phytate content and increasing Zn dialyzability, although further studies are needed to assess the effect of the treatment in the bioavailability of other minerals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the phytases produced by bifidobacteria can be successfully used in infant foods to reduce the content of phytate, thus increasing the availability of minerals, especially Zn.
bifidobacterial enzymes are safe and can be used in foods for human consumption.
bifidobacterial enzymes can be used as an alternative to fungal phytases for the dephytinization of infant cereals.
